commit.message:
Fix: name the step that failed when a skill bundle download fails (#1138) (#1141)

* Fix: name the step that failed when a skill bundle download fails (#1138)

Every remote bundle error was prefixed "Could not verify skill bundle",
so a network timeout read as a signature failure. The bundle path now
returns a BundleError tagged where it fails: Download (connect, HTTP
error status, stall, size cap), Verify (keyring, release pin, signature,
digest), Unpack (staging, read-back, extraction) or Local
(IMPECCABLE_BUNDLE_PATH). install keeps #734's fatal-on-remote rule via
is_remote() instead of a prefix check.

AI-assisted: prepared with Claude Code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Label a failed save of the downloaded bundle as unpack, not download

download_file_capped now returns BundleError itself: request, status,
redirect, body-read and size-cap failures are Download, while opening,
writing or flushing the destination file is Unpack. download_file_with
keeps its plain-string errors.

AI-assisted: prepared with Claude Code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Bundle layout `//skills//...`, `//agents/*.md`, hook manifests `/.claude/settings.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.github/hooks/impeccable.json`, `.grok/hooks/impeccable.json`. A failed remote bundle prints either `Could not download skill bundle: ${msg}` (the release lookup, signature, or ZIP request failed: connect error, HTTP status, stall, size cap), `Could not verify skill bundle: ${msg}` (keyring, release redirect or version check, signature envelope, key, signature, digest or size mismatch), or `Could not unpack skill bundle: ${msg}` (staging, saving, reading back or extracting the bundle on this machine), each followed by `. Nothing was installed; retry or update the CLI. If this persists, report it at https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/issues/new`. Fresh install: `stdout> \nDownloading impeccable skills...`; migrate `*-impeccable` prefixed dirs → `impeccable`; copy each skill dir (rm existing dest first; drop an in-project cross-provider symlinked skills dir); copy agents (`.github`→`.github/agents` or `~/.copilot/agents`; `.cursor`→`.cursor/agents` or `~/.cursor/agents`); write hooks (Claude project scope: `.claude/settings.local.json`, skipped when project `.claude/settings.json` already carries the marker; Claude user scope: `~/.claude/settings.json`, with obsolete Impeccable entries pruned from `~/.claude/settings.local.json`; other destinations: `.cursor/hooks.json`, `.codex/hooks.json` for `.agents`, `.github/hooks/impeccable.json`, `.grok/hooks/impeccable.json`); merged with existing JSON (`mergeHookManifests`: strips existing impeccable entries by markers `skills/impeccable/scripts/hook-probe.mjs|hook.mjs|hook-before-edit.mjs|hook-after-edit.mjs|hook-stop.mjs`, then appends fresh); invalid existing JSON → error `Existing hook manifest is not valid JSON: ${dest}. Re-run with --force to replace it.` (with `--force`, `.bak` written). Claude and Gemini user settings are never replaced wholesale when invalid. Hook command rewriting: `[ ! -f '' ] || node ''` (POSIX, single-quote-escaped) when absolute (user scope or global skill), else `[ ! -f "" ] || node ""` where rel = `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/hook.mjs` (Claude), `.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/hook.mjs` (Codex; plus `commandWindows: if exist "

" (node "

" & exit /b)`), `.cursor/skills/impeccable/scripts/hook-before-edit.mjs`; on win32 for non-Codex: `node -e "" ""`. Output: `Installed impeccable into: ${targets.join(', ')} (${'global'|'project'})`, optional `Installed agents into: ` (+ shadow warning), `Installed hooks into: ...`, then `\nDone! Now type /impeccable init in your AI coding agent's chat (not in this terminal) to set up design context.\n`. Errors: `Download failed: ...` / `Install failed: ...` / `Nothing was installed: the bundle had no variants for ...` → exit 1. A Claude user-scope hook write also prunes obsolete Impeccable entries from the current project's `.claude/settings.local.json`, preventing a stale project hook from firing alongside the user hook. GitHub Copilot hook (`.github/hooks/impeccable.json` in the project, `bash` key): a project install keeps the bundle's portable `$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/.github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable` command; a user-scope install rewrites it to the home launcher (`$HOME/.github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable` on POSIX, the resolved profile path with forward slashes on Windows), unless the project ships its own `.github/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable`, whose committed portable manifest is left as is. In user scope a project manifest that names the portable path while the project has no Copilot skill does not count as installed, so a repeat install rewrites it.
